label: bm-funding-materials
topic: Funding for responsive biomaterials and computational architecture
summary: Read on 2026-11-12. Most promising funded routes for a Lean-checked, Formlabs-printed responsive biomaterial offered to an architecture practice: (1) US, rolling: NSF 26-521 (Biomaterials and other MPS materials programmes; 1 proposal per person per fiscal year) and NSF 26-515 (CMMI: AMDO manufacturing, MAMS mechanics of engineered and biological materials), both 'Proposals Accepted Anytime', each about USD 100M for 200-300 awards (own mean 0.33-0.5M and 0.36-0.44M). (2) US, scheduled but unannounced: DMREF (USD 1.5-2.0M, 4 yr) is biennial in odd years; last window Jan 21-Feb 4 2025, next not published. NSF Future Manufacturing is closed (replacement promised for FY 2026, not found). (3) UK/EU with dated deadlines: NMIP Digital Materials Sandpit (closes 26 Nov 2026, UK research orgs), ERC Consolidator (12 Jan 2027), Innovate UK Investor Partnerships NMIP-1 (19 Jan 2027, UK SMEs), EIC Pathfinder Open (stage 1: 25 Feb 2027, up to EUR 4M, 3-country consortium), EPSRC responsive mode (no deadline, UK institutions). Crossref funder metadata for seven precedent hygromorph-architecture papers names SNSF, DFG, Innosuisse, DBU and EPSRC (no US agency). Private foundations in the brief are mostly closed doors (Autodesk invite-only; Schmidt no unsolicited; Simons LOI missed; Sloan unreadable; Holcim awards ended). Could not read any open DARPA, ARPA-E or DOE call. Earlier-file check: Flexible 80A V2's datasheet does give +8 percent mass in water at 1 day (confirming spec-formlabs-materials), which contradicts the blanket 'under 1 percent for every SLA resin' in spec-resin-chemistry; the two Formlabs documents disagree, and that disagreement is itself a fundable measurement question.
lay_summary: Researchers who want money for this kind of work mostly apply to science agencies, and each agency has its own calendar. In the United States the easiest doors right now are two National Science Foundation programmes that take applications at any time of year, each handing out a few hundred modest grants. The bigger prize, a multi-million-dollar materials-design grant, only opens every second year and the next date has not been announced. In the United Kingdom and Europe there are several dated deadlines between late November 2026 and February 2027, but most require a UK or European applicant. Think of it as a train timetable: some trains run all day, some leave in January, and a few have no published departure. Private foundations were mostly closed or invitation-only, so they are not a quick route.

glossary.plain: National Science Foundation, the main US government funder of basic science.
An NSF programme that funds teams who design new materials by looping between theory, computer simulation and experiments.
You can submit on any day; there is no single closing date.
The official document that describes a funding programme, its rules and its dates.
A short first application that a funder uses to decide whom to invite to submit a full one.
US small-business research grants; only companies can apply (STTR must partner with a university).
The UK council that funds engineering and physical sciences research.
The UK agency that funds business innovation projects.
Small or medium-sized enterprise, a company below a size limit.
A European Union programme for early, high-risk technology ideas, funded as consortia from several countries.
European Research Council, which funds single lead researchers for five-year projects.
A UK way of costing a project, including overheads; EPSRC pays 80 percent of it.
A material that bends or curls when it takes up or loses moisture, like a pine cone scale.
A mathematical statement that a proof-checking program (Lean) has verified step by step.
The list of funders that a paper's publisher recorded for that paper.

findings.claim: DMREF awards are USD 1.5-2.0M over four years and the programme expects competitions every two years, in odd-numbered years, subject to funds.
findings.evidence_quote: Awards are expected to range from $1,500,000 – $2,000,000 over a duration of four years. Subject to the availability of funds, it is anticipated that the DMREF program will continue with competitions biennially in odd-numbered years.

findings.claim: The last DMREF submission window (NSF 25-508) ran 21 January to 4 February 2025; I found no later DMREF solicitation, so the next deadline is not published (my inference from the odd-year rule: a window in early 2027).
findings.evidence_quote: The submission window is January 21-February 4, 2025, closing at 5 p.m. submitting organization's local time.

findings.claim: DMREF requires a team of at least two senior/key personnel and a closed-loop process in which theory guides computation, which guides experiment.
findings.evidence_quote: Proposals submitted to this solicitation must be directed by a team of at least two Senior/Key Personnel with complementary expertise.

findings.claim: DMREF 25-508 planned 20-25 awards from USD 40M; own arithmetic 40M/25 = 1.6M and 40M/20 = 2.0M, consistent with the stated 1.5-2.0M range.
findings.evidence_quote: Estimated Number of Awards: 20 to 25 The number of awards will depend on the availability of funds and the quality of the proposals. Anticipated Funding Amount: $40,000,000

findings.claim: Pattern: every named funder in this small sample is European (Swiss, German, UK); none is a US agency. Sample is tiny and Crossref funder data is incomplete, so this is a pointer, not a proof.

CONFIRMED and located: Flexible 80A Resin V2's own datasheet (ASTM D471, rectangular slabs, wiped dry) lists deionized water at 1 day: -26 Shore A, +8 percent mass, +3 percent volume; 1 week: +9 percent mass, +7 percent volume. Matches spec-formlabs-materials.json. Read with pdftotext -raw; -layout scrambles the table, so label-to-row alignment is inferred (label above its data; Bleach 1-week 'N/A' fits that reading).

CONTRADICTION to a blanket claim in spec-resin-chemistry.json ('every current Formlabs SLA resin gains under 1 percent mass in water at 24 h'): Formlabs' own datasheet for Flexible 80A V2 gives +8 percent at one day. The two Formlabs documents differ: solvent page = printed 1 cm cubes, 24 h, post-cured, row 'Flexible 80A Resin' (no V2 label); datasheet = ASTM D471 slabs wiped dry. I cannot say which is right; both stand as stated by Formlabs. Matters for funding because an unresolved 10-fold disagreement is a concrete, fundable measurement aim.
findings.evidence_quote: Formlabs measures resistance to solvents by observing, measuring, and weighing printed cubes (originally measuring 1 cm × 1 cm × 1 cm) before and after immersion in a solvent for 24 hours.

findings.claim: DEEPENED: the 'no hygroscopic expansion coefficient or diffusivity for any Formlabs resin' gap is exactly what NSF 26-521 BMAT/POL and NSF 26-515 MAMS describe funding ('foundational research'); a proposal can frame the measurement of those two constants plus the 3/2 curvature ceiling as the foundational question. This is my judgement, not a statement by NSF.

No funder page read mentions Formlabs, vat-photopolymer hygromorphs, or Lean-checked material laws; I found no programme that funds 'machine-checked constraints on a material' as such. The framing must be bridged: formal verification as a design-loop component (DMREF) or as foundational mechanics (MAMS).

key_claims.claim: The two lowest-barrier US routes right now are rolling NSF solicitations posted 17 Aug 2026: NSF 26-521 (Biomaterials/Polymers/etc., 1 proposal per person per fiscal year) and NSF 26-515 (CMMI: AMDO manufacturing, MAMS mechanics of engineered and biological materials, no per-PI limit). Both accept proposals at any time.
key_claims.evidence_quote: Full Proposal Deadline(s) (due by 5 p.m. submitting organization's local time): Proposals Accepted Anytime

key_claims.claim: The big NSF design-of-materials programme, DMREF (USD 1.5-2.0M over 4 years), has no open deadline: last window was 21 Jan-4 Feb 2025, recurrence is biennial in odd years, and no 2027 solicitation was found. NSF Future Manufacturing is closed with a replacement promised for FY 2026 but not found.
key_claims.evidence_quote: Subject to the availability of funds, it is anticipated that the DMREF program will continue with competitions biennially in odd-numbered years.

key_claims.claim: The nearest dated European/UK deadlines are: NMIP Digital Materials Sandpit 26 Nov 2026 (UK research orgs), ERC Consolidator 12 Jan 2027, Innovate UK Investor Partnerships 19 Jan 2027 (UK SMEs), EIC Pathfinder Open Stage 1 on 25 Feb 2027 (EUR up to 4M, 3-country consortium). All need a UK/EU-based applicant; a US-only team is not eligible for the UK ones.
key_claims.evidence_quote: Deadline for submitting your proposal: EIC Pathfinder Open Stage 1: 25 February 2027 Stage 2 : 16 September 2027

key_claims.claim: Private foundations in the brief do not offer an open door: Autodesk Foundation is invite-only, Schmidt Sciences takes no unsolicited proposals, Simons' MPS collaboration LOI closed 29 Oct 2026, Sloan and Holcim could not be used; only Graham (small, architecture-led, 25 Feb 2027 for organisations) is open.
key_claims.evidence_quote: We proactively seek out grant opportunities and do not accept unsolicited proposals.

recommendations: Now-ish (US): pick ONE of NSF 26-521 (BMAT/POL) or NSF 26-515 (MAMS/AMDO) for a rolling submission; 26-521 allows one proposal per person per fiscal year so the choice matters; contact the listed programme team (bmat/pol or cmmi-mams/cmmi-amdo mailboxes on the solicitation) with a one-page summary before writing.
Prepare, do not yet write, a DMREF proposal: watch the DMREF page for the next solicitation (expected odd-year window, early 2027 by the pattern); needs two or more senior personnel.

Run the cheap measurement first (Flexible 80A V2 vs Silicone 40A or Rigid 10K, humid-air and immersion swelling, plus diffusivity): the Formlabs cube-test vs datasheet disagreement (0.7 vs +8 percent) is the concrete preliminary result every programme above will want.

If the architecture partner is UK-based, test whether a UK university PI would co-lead an EPSRC responsive-mode grant (no deadline) and whether the practice is an eligible SME for Innovate UK Investor Partnerships (closes 19 Jan 2027, needs private investor money).
For a European consortium route, EIC Pathfinder Open stage 1 (25 Feb 2027) is the only large dated target with a fit; it needs three partner countries.
Do not spend effort on Autodesk Foundation, Schmidt, Simons or Holcim now; revisit Graham (25 Feb 2027) only for a small exhibition/prototype grant led by the practice.
Re-read the DARPA/ARPA-E/DOE listings by hand in a browser (JavaScript pages) before ruling them out.
